THE SHADOW GAME
Connecting the Dots from the Old Testament to Jesus
Christine A.
Illustrated by [Illustrator Name]

A Note for Parents


Have you ever played a game of connect the dots? You start with a bunch of dots on a page. They look like random dots. They look like nothing. But then you draw a line from one dot to the next. And then to the next. And slowly, a picture appears. It was there all along. You just had to connect the dots.


The Old Testament is like a connect the dots page. There are stories. There are people. There are rules. There are ceremonies. They can seem random. They can seem disconnected. They can seem like they do not have anything to do with Jesus. But they do. Every dot connects. Every story connects. Every person connects. They all point to Jesus. They all draw a picture of Him. The picture was there all along. We just have to connect the dots.


This book is a 30 day adventure for you and your kids. We are going to play the shadow game. We are going to look at 30 Old Testament dots. We are going to connect them to Jesus. We are going to see the picture. Get ready to draw. Get ready to connect. Get ready to find Jesus.


How to Use This Book


This is a 30 day journey. Each day takes about 5 to 10 minutes. Read the shadow. Read the connection. Do the family activity together. Say the prayer out loud. Let your child color the picture. pages.body:
The Shadow
"Consecrate to me every firstborn male. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or animal." - Exodus 13:2


In the Old Testament, the firstborn was special. The firstborn got the double portion. The firstborn got the blessing. The firstborn got the authority. But God said the firstborn belonged to Him. Why? Because God saved the firstborn of Israel during the Passover. The firstborn was a reminder. It was a dot. It was a shadow.


The Connection
"For those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brothers and sisters." - Romans 8:29


Connect the dot. The firstborn points to Jesus. Jesus is the firstborn. He is the firstborn of all creation. He is the firstborn from the dead. He is the firstborn among many brothers and sisters. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Make a list of the firstborns in your family. Talk about how the firstborn was special in the Old Testament. Talk about how Jesus is the firstborn. He is the special one. He is the one who saves us.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the firstborn. Thank you for making me part of the family. Thank you for saving me. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A family with a big heart in the middle.

The Shadow
"Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old. You may take it from the sheep or from the goats." - Exodus 12:5


In the Old Testament, the lamb was special. It had to be perfect. It had to be without spot. It had to be without blemish. It had to be killed. It had to be eaten. The lamb was a dot. The lamb was a shadow.


The Connection
"Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" - John 1:29


Connect the dot. The lamb points to Jesus. Jesus is the Lamb of God. He is perfect. He is without spot. He is without blemish. He was killed. He was sacrificed. He takes away the sin of the world. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Draw a picture of a lamb. Add a big heart on the lamb. Talk about how the lamb had to be perfect. Talk about how Jesus is the perfect Lamb. He gave His life for us.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the perfect Lamb. Thank you for taking away my sin. Thank you for loving me. I love you. Amen."

A fluffy white lamb with a big smile.

The Shadow
"The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you." - Exodus 12:13


In the Old Testament, the blood was special. It was a sign. It was a protection. It was a covering. The blood was painted on the doorposts. The blood saved the people. The blood was a dot. The blood was a shadow.


The Connection
"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed." - 1 Corinthians 5:7


Connect the dot. The blood points to Jesus. Jesus is our Passover Lamb. He shed His blood for us. His blood is on the door of our hearts. His blood protects us. His blood saves us. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Cut out a paper door. Color it red. Tape it to your child's bedroom door. Talk about how the blood saved the people. Talk about how the blood of Jesus saves us. Every time you see the door, say, "Jesus saves me."


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for your blood. Thank you for saving me. Thank you for protecting me. I love you. Amen."

A door painted with a red stripe.

The Shadow
"For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast." - Exodus 12:15


In the Old Testament, the bread was special. It had to be unleavened. It had to be without yeast. Yeast was a symbol of sin. Yeast spreads. Yeast puffs up. The bread was a dot. The bread was a shadow.


The Connection
"I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty." - John 6:35


Connect the dot. The bread points to Jesus. Jesus is the Bread of Life. He is without yeast. He is without sin. He is pure. He feeds us. He satisfies us. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Bake a simple flatbread together. Or buy some pita bread. Talk about how the bread is flat because it has no yeast. Talk about how Jesus is pure like the flatbread. Jesus is the Bread of Life.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the Bread of Life. Thank you for feeding me. Thank you for satisfying me. I love you. Amen."

In the Old Testament, the shoes were special. The people had to eat the Passover with their shoes on. They had to be ready to move. They had to be ready to go. The shoes were a dot. The shoes were a shadow.


The Connection

Connect the dot. The shoes point to Jesus. Jesus calls us to be ready. He is coming back. He wants us to be prepared. He wants us to be watching. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.

Kid's Prayer

"Eat the meat roasted over the fire, along with bitter herbs." - Exodus 12:8


In the Old Testament, the bitter herbs were special. They were a reminder. They reminded the people of their slavery. They reminded them of their pain. The bitter herbs were a dot. The bitter herbs were a shadow.

"It is a night of watching for the LORD, to bring them out of Egypt." - Exodus 12:42


In the Old Testament, the night of watching was special. The people were awake. The people were waiting. The people were watching. They were waiting for God to deliver them. The night of watching was a dot. The night of watching was a shadow.


The Connection

Connect the dot. The night of watching points to Jesus. Jesus is the one we watch for. He is the one we wait for. He is coming back. We need to be on our guard. We need to be watching. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity

Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the one I watch for. Help me to be on my guard. Help me to be watching. I love you. Amen."

"This is a day you are to commemorate; for the generations to come you shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD—a lasting ordinance." - Exodus 12:14


In the Old Testament, the memorial was special. The people were told to remember. They were told to remember what God had done. They were told to remember the day of deliverance. The memorial was a dot. The memorial was a shadow.


The Connection
"Do this in remembrance of me." - 1 Corinthians 11:24

Family Activity

Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for remembering me. Help me to remember you. Help me to remember your sacrifice. Help me to remember your love. I love you. Amen."

The Shadow
"Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove the sea back with a strong east wind and turned it into dry land." - Exodus 14:21


In the Old Testament, the Red Sea was special. It was a barrier. It was an obstacle. It was a problem. The people could not cross it. They were trapped. But God parted the sea. He made a way. The Red Sea was a dot. The Red Sea was a shadow.


The Connection
"So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." - John 8:36


Connect the dot. The Red Sea points to Jesus. Jesus is the one who makes a way. He parts the impossible. He sets us free. He brings us out of slavery. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Fill a bowl with water. Use two stiff pieces of cardboard to part the water. Talk about how God parted the Red Sea. Talk about how Jesus parts the impossible in our lives. He makes a way for us.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for making a way for me. Thank you for parting the impossible. Thank you for setting me free. I love you. Amen."

The Shadow
"I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink." - Exodus 17:6


In the Old Testament, the rock was special. It was a source of water. It was a source of life. The people were thirsty. They were complaining. God told Moses to strike the rock. Moses struck the rock. Water came out. The rock was a dot. The rock was a shadow.


The Connection
"They all drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ." - 1 Corinthians 10:4


Connect the dot. The rock points to Jesus. Jesus is the spiritual rock. He is the source of living water. He is the one who satisfies our thirsty souls. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.

pages.body:
The Shadow
"So Moses made a bronze snake and put it up on a pole. Then when anyone was bitten by a snake and looked at the bronze snake, they lived." - Numbers 21:9


In the Old Testament, the bronze serpent was special. The people were dying. They were bitten by snakes. God told Moses to make a bronze snake. He told him to put it on a pole. Whoever looked at it would live. The bronze serpent was a dot. The bronze serpent was a shadow.


The Connection
"Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him." - John 3:14-15


Connect the dot. The bronze serpent points to Jesus. Jesus was lifted up on a cross. He was raised up on a pole. Whoever looks at Him will live. Whoever believes in Him will have eternal life. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Put a stuffed animal on a high shelf. Tell your child to look at it when they feel sad. Talk about how the people looked at the bronze snake and lived. Talk about how we look at Jesus and live.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being lifted up for me. Thank you for the promise that whoever looks at you will live. I am looking at you. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A wooden pole with a bronze snake and a big smile.
pages.title: Day 13: The Shadow of the Bronze Serpent

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Shadow
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'Select some towns to be your cities of refuge, to which a person who has killed someone accidentally may flee.'" - Numbers 35:10-11


In the Old Testament, the cities of refuge were special. They were safe places. They were places of protection. If someone killed a person by accident, they could flee to a city of refuge. They were safe. The cities of refuge were a dot. The cities of refuge were a shadow.


The Connection
"Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus." - Romans 8:1


Connect the dot. The cities of refuge point to Jesus. Jesus is our city of refuge. He is our safe place. He is our protection. When we run to Him, we are safe. We are not condemned. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Build a fort with blankets. Crawl inside with your child. Talk about how the cities of refuge were safe places. Talk about how Jesus is our safe place. We can run to Him.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being my city of refuge. Thank you for being my safe place. Thank you for protecting me. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A fort with a big heart on it.
pages.title: Day 14: The Shadow of the Cities of Refuge

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Shadow
"Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy. Six days you shall labor and do all your work, but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God." - Exodus 20:8-10


In the Old Testament, the Sabbath was special. It was a day of rest. It was a day of ceasing. The people were told to stop working. They were told to rest. The Sabbath was a dot. The Sabbath was a shadow.


The Connection
"Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest." - Matthew 11:28


Connect the dot. The Sabbath points to Jesus. Jesus is our rest. He is the one who gives us peace. He is the one who gives us rest. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Have a day of rest. Take a nap. Read a book. Go for a walk. Talk about how God wants us to rest. Talk about how Jesus is our rest. We can rest in Him.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being my rest. Thank you for giving me peace. Thank you for giving me rest. I love you. Amen."

A person sleeping peacefully with a big smile.
pages.title: Day 15: The Shadow of the Sabbath

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Shadow
"Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family property and to your own clan." - Leviticus 25:10


In the Old Testament, the Jubilee was special. It was a year of freedom. It was a year of release. It was a year of restoration. Every fifty years, the Israelites were to proclaim liberty. Slaves were set free. Debts were cancelled. The Jubilee was a dot. The Jubilee was a shadow.


The Connection
"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and recovery of sight for the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor." - Luke 4:18-19


Connect the dot. The Jubilee points to Jesus. Jesus is our Jubilee. He is our freedom. He is our release. He is our restoration. He proclaims good news to the poor. He sets the oppressed free. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Ring a bell. Shout "Freedom!" Talk about how the Jubilee was a year of freedom. Talk about how Jesus sets us free. We can be free because of Him.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being my Jubilee. Thank you for proclaiming freedom to me. Thank you for releasing me from bondage. Thank you for restoring me. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A bell with a big smile.
pages.title: Day 16: The Shadow of the Jubilee

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey

The Shadow
"This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month you must deny yourselves and not do any work—whether native-born or a foreigner residing among you—because on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you." - Leviticus 16:29-30


In the Old Testament, the Day of Atonement was special. It was the holiest day of the year. It was a day of fasting. It was a day of sacrifice. It was a day of cleansing. The Day of Atonement was a dot. The Day of Atonement was a shadow.


The Connection
"He did not enter by means of the blood of goats and calves; but he entered the Most Holy Place once for all by his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption." - Hebrews 9:12


Connect the dot. The Day of Atonement points to Jesus. Jesus is our Day of Atonement. He is our High Priest. He is our sacrifice. He entered the Most Holy Place once for all. He obtained eternal redemption. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Talk about a time you needed to be cleansed. Talk about how Jesus cleanses us. He made atonement for us. Once. For all. We can be clean because of Him.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being my Day of Atonement. Thank you for entering the Most Holy Place. Thank you for obtaining eternal redemption. Thank you for cleansing me. I love you. Amen."

pages.title: Day 17: The Shadow of the Day of Atonement

The Shadow
"He is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the wickedness and rebellion of the Israelites—all their sins—and put them on the goat's head. He shall send the goat away into the wilderness." - Leviticus 16:21


In the Old Testament, the scapegoat was special. The high priest laid his hands on it. He confessed the sins of the people. He put the sins on the goat's head. He sent the goat away. The scapegoat was a dot. The scapegoat was a shadow.


The Connection
"We all, like sheep, have gone astray, each of us has turned to our own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all." - Isaiah 53:6


Connect the dot. The scapegoat points to Jesus. Jesus is our scapegoat. The sins of the world were laid on Him. He carried them away. He took them to the cross. He took them to the grave. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Write a mistake on a piece of paper. Tie it to a balloon. Let the balloon go. Talk about how the scapegoat carried the sins away. Talk about how Jesus carries our sins away. They are gone.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for carrying my sins away. Thank you for taking them to the cross. Thank you for removing them. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A goat with a big heart on it.
pages.title: Day 18: The Shadow of the Scapegoat

The Shadow
"I have indeed built a magnificent temple for you, a place for you to dwell forever." - 1 Kings 8:13


In the Old Testament, the temple was special. It was the dwelling place of God. It was where God met with His people. It was where the sacrifices were made. The temple was a dot. The temple was a shadow.


The Connection
"Jesus answered them, 'Destroy this temple, and I will raise it again in three days.' But the temple he had spoken of was his body." - John 2:19-21


Connect the dot. The temple points to Jesus. Jesus is the temple. He is the dwelling place of God. He is the meeting place. He is the sacrifice. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Build a temple out of blocks. Talk about how the temple was the dwelling place of God. Talk about how Jesus is the temple. He is the dwelling place of God. We meet God in Him.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the temple. Thank you for being the dwelling place of God. Thank you for being the meeting place. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A beautiful building with a big heart on it.
pages.title: Day 19: The Shadow of the Temple

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Shadow
"The LORD said to Moses: 'Tell your brother Aaron that he is not to come whenever he chooses into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain in front of the atonement cover on the ark, or else he will die.'" - Leviticus 16:2


In the Old Testament, the high priest was special. He was the mediator. He was the go-between. He represented the people before God. He offered sacrifices. He made atonement. The high priest was a dot. The high priest was a shadow.


The Connection
"Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has ascended into heaven, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to the faith we profess." - Hebrews 4:14


Connect the dot. The high priest points to Jesus. Jesus is our High Priest. He is our mediator. He is our go-between. He represents us before God. He intercedes for us. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Talk about how the high priest had to be careful. Talk about how Jesus is our High Priest. He entered the Most Holy Place for us. He made a way. We can come to God because of Him.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being my High Priest. Thank you for representing me before God. Thank you for interceding for me. I love you. Amen."

A high priest with a big heart on his chest.
pages.title: Day 20: The Shadow of the High Priest

"The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your fellow Israelites. You must listen to him." - Deuteronomy 18:15


In the Old Testament, the prophet was special. He was the messenger. He was the voice of God. He spoke God's words. He told the people what God wanted them to know. The prophet was a dot. The prophet was a shadow.


The Connection

Connect the dot. The prophet points to Jesus. Jesus is the ultimate prophet. He is the voice of God. He speaks God's words. He tells us what God wants us to know. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Play a game of "telephone." Whisper a message to your child. Let them whisper it to someone else. Talk about how the prophets spoke God's words. Talk about how Jesus is the ultimate prophet. He speaks God's words to us.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the ultimate prophet. Thank you for speaking God's words. Thank you for telling me what God wants me to know. I love you. Amen."

The Shadow
"The LORD is my shepherd, I lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures, he leads me beside quiet waters." - Psalm 23:1-2


In the Old Testament, the shepherd was special. He was the guide. He was the protector. He was the provider. He led the sheep. He protected the sheep. He provided for the sheep. The shepherd was a dot. The shepherd was a shadow.


The Connection
"I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep." - John 10:11


Connect the dot. The shepherd points to Jesus. Jesus is the Good Shepherd. He is our guide. He is our protector. He is our provider. He leads us. He protects us. He provides for us. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Draw a picture of a shepherd with his sheep. Talk about how the shepherd leads and protects his sheep. Talk about how Jesus is our Good Shepherd. He leads us. He protects us. He provides for us.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being my Good Shepherd. Thank you for leading me. Thank you for protecting me. Thank you for providing for me. I love you. Amen."

The Shadow
"Aaron must burn fragrant incense on the altar every morning when he tends the lamps." - Exodus 30:7


In the Old Testament, the incense was special. It was a sweet smell. It was burned every morning. It was burned on the altar. It filled the tabernacle. It rose to heaven. It was a picture of prayer. The incense was a dot. The incense was a shadow.


The Connection
"The smoke of the incense, together with the prayers of God's people, went up before God from the angel's hand." - Revelation 8:4


Connect the dot. The incense points to Jesus. Jesus is the one who prays for us. He is the one who intercedes for us. His prayers rise to heaven. Our prayers rise to heaven because of Him. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Smell a sweet candle or flower. Talk about how the incense was a sweet smell. Talk about how our prayers rise to heaven. Jesus is the one who prays for us.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for praying for me. Thank you for interceding for me. Thank you for making my prayers rise to heaven. I love you. Amen."

The Shadow
"Hang the curtain from the clasps and place the ark of the covenant law behind the curtain. The curtain will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place." - Exodus 26:33


In the Old Testament, the veil was special. It was a thick curtain. It separated the people from the Most Holy Place. It separated them from the presence of God. The veil was a dot. The veil was a shadow.


The Connection
"At that moment the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom." - Matthew 27:51


Connect the dot. The veil points to Jesus. The veil separated the people from God. When Jesus died, the veil was torn in two. The barrier was removed. The separation was ended. The dot connects to Jesus. The picture is Jesus.


Family Activity
Take a piece of paper. Talk about how it separates you from something. Then rip the paper in half. Talk about how the veil was torn when Jesus died. We can come to God now. We have access.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for removing the barrier. Thank you for tearing the veil. Thank you for giving me access to God. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A torn curtain with a big heart.
pages.title: Day 29: The Shadow of the Veil

pages.body:
The Shadow
"These are a shadow of the things that were to come; the reality, however, is found in Christ." - Colossians 2:17


All the dots were shadows. They were clues. They were pointing to something. They were pointing to someone. They were pointing to Jesus. When we connect the dots, we see the picture. The picture is Jesus.


The Connection
"For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed." - 1 Corinthians 5:7


Jesus is the real picture. He is the fulfillment of every shadow. He is the meaning behind every dot. He is the treasure at the end of the hunt. When we connect the dots, we find Jesus. He was there all along.


Family Activity
Draw a picture using dots. Connect the dots to reveal the picture. Talk about how the Old Testament is like a connect the dots page. When we connect the dots, we see Jesus. We found Him. We love Him. We thank Him.


Kid's Prayer
"Thank you, Jesus, for being the real picture. Thank you for being the fulfillment of every shadow. Thank you for being the treasure. Help me to live in the reality. Help me to live in you. I love you. Amen."


Coloring Prompt
A big picture of Jesus with a big smile.

A Note for the Parent: Building on the Foundation


You did it. You spent 30 days connecting the dots from the Old Testament to Jesus. But the adventure does not end here. It is just beginning.


Here are a few tips to keep going:


1. Make it a habit, not a chore. Do not stress about reading the Bible for 30 minutes a day. A simple 5 minute rhythm before bed is better than an hour once a month.
2. Let them see you reading. Kids do what they see. Let them catch you reading your Bible. Let them see that it matters to you.
3. Ask "Where is Jesus?" in every story. Whenever you read a Bible story, ask your child, "Where do you see Jesus in this story?" This trains them to look for Jesus everywhere.
4. Recommended next steps. Read The Jesus Storybook Bible by Sally Lloyd-Jones. Read The Biggest Story by Kevin DeYoung. Keep pointing them to the Treasure.


You are doing a great job. Keep going.
